reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents a cryptocurrency mining and leasing platform as a way to earn Litecoin through stable fixed daily income and product-specific returns tied to purchasing or leasing computing power. It directs viewers to register, use an invitation code, and fund the platform with cryptocurrency, linking participation and deposits to the promoted products and returns. Although a personal-thoughts disclaimer provides countercontext, the available video evidence states that no transfer, payout, or user loss was established.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker's claims about returns should be read alongside the creator's express allocation of responsibility to viewers. The description says these are personal thoughts, disclaims investment advice, and puts the decision on the viewer. That does not prove the mining claims are sound, but it matters when deciding whether the video presents them as an independently verified promise. The speaker also says the withdrawal process will be shown in a later video. This record therefore contains a discussion of stated rates, not a demonstrated payout that the viewer is asked to treat as proven.

citations.quote: I express my personal thoughts in all my videos, there is no investment advice in any way, the responsibility is entirely yours.
We will do all these processes in my second video guys.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening accurately identifies mining purchases and advertised rates, but those facts alone do not establish that the advertised income was paid or that a viewer lost funds. Even the speaker's account of the test ends with a promise to share results later. The cited withdrawal instruction describes a procedure, not evidence of a completed withdrawal. The disclaimer does not verify the platform, but it does qualify how the creator presents the discussion.

citations.quote: I want to buy this product for three days and I'm share my results and I will make another which little video after three days
there is no investment advice in any way, the responsibility is entirely yours.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer cannot neutralize the concrete offer being promoted. The description promises stable, fixed daily income from purchasing cloud computing power, while the speaker tells viewers they can register with his invitation code and demonstrates funding and buying a product. No completed payout is needed to recognize that the video promotes paid mining returns; the promised later withdrawal demonstration does not change what this video asks viewers to consider doing.

opening.argument: Judge, this is structured as a walk-through of an interface and a small first-person test. The speaker introduces a review of products and commission rates, shows how recharging works, then says he will try one pool for three days and report results afterward. He also points to account and withdrawal controls without showing that a withdrawal succeeded. A tutorial can display a platform's advertised rates without independently endorsing their accuracy; the unfinished test is important context for interpreting what the video establishes.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening treats the registration, funding, and product screens as a solicitation. Yet the same transcript presents a sequence of interface demonstrations and postpones the outcome. Its rate quotes establish what the platform advertises, not whether mining occurred or returns were received. The registration screen likewise establishes a displayed workflow; it does not, by itself, resolve whether the speaker's primary purpose is instruction or promotion.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The demonstration framing omits its most consequential steps: the speaker supplies an invitation code, walks through sending funds, reports a balance, and says he bought the mining product. The description supplies the economic pitch, including fixed daily income and minimum lease amounts. Showing an interface does not make those actions merely educational when the walk-through connects registration and funding to the advertised returns.

opening.argument: Judge, the visible offer can also be understood as a paid service with stated lease terms: the description names minimum amounts, durations, and rates for different pools, and the product interface presents a lease action. The speaker discusses referral commissions as a separate platform feature, but the record does not show that recruiting others is required to purchase a lease. Nor does it show a completed payout, a failed payout, or misuse of an account. Those missing outcomes do not certify the service as safe; they limit what can be inferred from this video alone about its operation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening establishes that the advertised service involves payment and daily returns; it does not establish whether the computing power exists or whether a lease ever pays out. The speaker's referral explanation also does not show recruitment as a condition of using the product. The funding and withdrawal screens are consistent with an account-based purchase workflow, although they provide no independent assurance that the service works as advertised.

citations.quote: Users can earn Litecoin by purchasing cloud computing power and leasing mining.
You can also get some rebates by inviting people

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling this a lease does not remove the central financial proposition: users are asked to pay for supposed mining power in exchange for fixed daily income, with higher stated rates at larger minimum amounts. The speaker demonstrates the recharge and says a product purchase succeeded. Recruitment need not be mandatory, and a failed payout need not be documented, for the video to be promoting that paid-return arrangement. The missing independent outcome is a reason not to certify the service, not a reason to treat the pitch as ordinary commerce.
